text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Leaders of public sector workers OeTV trade union says it is ready for battle under the banner: "The hot autumn (of industrial action) has begun".
- European truck manufacturers hope for new and good business
- Row over insurance for holidaymakers in case travel agents go bankrupt
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Row over cuts in sick pay. Public sector workers union OeTV refuses to accept pay cuts.
- Run-off local elections in regional state of Lower Saxony
- Family Minister Claudia Nolte bans some internet pages to protect young people from right-wing extremist propaganda
- German President Roman Herzog declares "merciless" war on corruption
- Bremen city-state is considering giving troubled ship builder Bremer Vulkan more financial aid
- International and national committee will be occupied this week with the difficult path to European monetary union
HANDELSBLATT
- Trade unionists threaten battle over work and vow to fight sick pay cuts
- Economy in eastern Germany is growing again
- Ruling coalition of Christian Democrats (CDU) and Bavarian sister party Christian Social Union (CSU) wants to reduce maximum income tax rate to 40 percent
- Former president of Bundesbank Karl Otto Pohl says the Maastricht criteria to qualify for a single currency should not become a dogma
- German upper house of parliament approved access to network for private telecommunications firms
- Ruhrgas AG is optimistic that natural gas can maintain its position in the market
DIE WELT
- Trade unionists vote for "hot autumn"
- German President Roman Herzog tells east Germans they can be proud of themselves days before the sixth anniversary of German unification
